record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.context_brief: Maximum hidden sets with boundary order
record.original_question: Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P together with the Hamiltonian cycle of G corresponding to the boundary of P, determine a maximum hidden set of G, meaning a largest set of vertices no two of which are adjacent.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 36 Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon P along with the Hamiltonian cycle in G corresponding to the boundary of P , determine the maximum hidden set of G.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a simple polygon in the plane with vertices v_1, v_2, ..., v_n listed in the cyclic order in which they appear along the boundary of P. The visibility graph G = G(P) has vertex set {v_1, ..., v_n}, with an edge between v_i and v_j whenever the open line segment v_i v_j lies entirely in the interior of P, or v_i v_j is an edge of the polygon boundary. Note that the boundary edges of P form a Hamiltonian cycle of G, and this cyclic order is given as part of the input.

A hidden set in G is a subset S of vertices such that no two vertices of S are adjacent in G (equivalently, an independent set of G). The size of a maximum hidden set is the independence number α(G).

Problem: Given as input the visibility graph G together with the Hamiltonian cycle of G specifying the boundary order of P, design an algorithm that computes a maximum hidden set of G, and determine the computational complexity of this problem.
artifact.status_search_result: The maximum hidden set problem in simple polygons is known to be NP-hard and hard to approximate within n^ε in geometric formulations. However, the combinatorial version asking for a maximum hidden set given the visibility graph together with its boundary Hamiltonian cycle remains open in terms of an exact polynomial-time algorithm or a matching hardness result; recent work (e.g., 2024) gives only constant-factor approximations (1/2-approximation) for related polygon settings, indicating the problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: An Overview of Minimum Convex Cover and Maximum Hidden Set
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work provides a 2-approximation for minimum convex cover and a 1/2-approximation for maximum hidden set in simple polygons.
status_evidence.claim: Only approximation algorithms are known; exact polynomial-time algorithm not established.

status_evidence.title: Visibility graph - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys results on visibility graphs of polygons, including hidden set/independent-set problems.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates ongoing open status for hidden set computation given visibility graph plus boundary Hamiltonian cycle.
